sources.title: Candles, Roman, 500 BCE — Smith College Museum of Ancient Inventions
The illuminating history of lighting — English Heritage

notes: 有芯蜡烛、盛油容器和浸脂灯草的边界会影响起源叙述。史密斯学院教学资料把罗马浸制蜡烛标为约前500年，英国遗产机构也以推测措辞归于罗马人；本条采用这一传统性年代作为展示点，不认定罗马是全球唯一发明地，也不把更早的灯草直接等同于蜡烛。13世纪的行会节点不是首次普及的精确年份。
notes_en: The boundaries between candles with wicks, oil-filled vessels and fat-soaked rushlights affect origin accounts. Smith College teaching material dates Roman dipped candles to around 500 BCE; English Heritage also cautiously attributes them to the Romans. This entry uses that conventional date as a display point, not a claim that Rome was the sole global birthplace or that earlier rushlights were candles. The 13th-century guild milestone is not an exact year of first widespread adoption.
summary_zh: 蜡烛把可燃脂或蜡包在灯芯周围，成为可携带的光源。罗马浸制烛是一条早期传统；到13世纪，英格兰和法国的制烛业已形成行会手艺。
summary_en: Candles surround a wick with solid fat or wax. Roman dipping is an early tradition; by the 13th century candle-making was a guild craft in England and France.
summary_ja: ろうそくは、芯を固形の脂や蝋で包んだものである。ローマでは早くから浸し掛けによる製法が使われ、13世紀にはイングランドとフランスで、ろうそく作りがギルドの手工業として営まれていた。
